title: I built a full browser football manager in a single HTML file using AI coding agents – here's what worked and what didn't
author: Erdal3666
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev!



I'm a software engineer and I've been building Global Football Manager 2026-27, a free browser-based football manager game, mostly by pair-programming with AI agents in Cursor.



Play it here (free, runs in the browser): [https://gfm-2026.itch.io/global-football-manager2026-2027](https://gfm-2026.itch.io/global-football-manager2026-2027)



What's in the game

• Real-time live match engine with live standings

• Domestic leagues across many countries, domestic cups and three European competitions (group stage + knockouts)

• AI managers that pick tactics based on squad strength relative to their league (strong teams attack, weaker teams park the bus)

• Finances, transfers, contracts, staff, facilities and weekly training/youth development



How AI was used

• The whole game lives in one big HTML file (tens of thousands of lines). The agent works directly on it: I describe a feature or bug in plain language, it finds the relevant code, edits it, and tests it.

• The agent tests changes itself in a real browser: it starts a local server, simulates days/weeks in a throwaway career and takes screenshots to check the UI.

• Balancing is a big part of it: e.g. I asked "when does a 50 OVR / 80 POT 16-year-old reach 80?", and the agent simulated the training formulas to answer, which led to rebalancing XP and growth caps.



Lessons learned

• Small, concrete requests (with a screenshot) work far better than vague "make it better" prompts.

• A single huge file is surprisingly workable for an agent, but you need syntax checks after every edit.

• Economy/balance bugs are the hardest: the agent fixes the formula, but you only see the real effect after simulating a full season.



Happy to answer questions about the workflow, and I'd love feedback on the game itself!
